Latest Update: Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m.
  • An eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO.
  • The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.

An eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.

The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their newly introduced teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.

Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:.

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

Industry observers note that CBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.

In a recent development, it must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams.

Industry observers note that free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.

The QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.

The current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.

One of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a new closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.

According to recent reports, there had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a significant win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup.

Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards went down after four games, I ranked it as the biggest injury blow any team has suffered this season, which was saying a lot given all the injuries we've seen.
  • Sources indicate that how are they doing it?
  • And by elite, we mean the best in the league.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards went down after four games, I ranked it as the biggest injury blow any team has suffered this season, which was saying a lot given all the injuries we've seen. As it turned out, Oklahoma City's barrage of injuries, Kawhi Leonard in Toronto, Tyrese Haliburton in Indiana, Jaren Jackson Jr. in Utah, Paolo Banchero in Orlando, and now Stephen Curry with the Warriors have all turned out to be significantly more debilitating as Minnesota has gone 8-3 without Edwards.

Sources indicate that how are they doing it? Let's take a look.

And by elite, we mean the best in the league. Minnesota is surrendering just 104 points per 100 possessions. Give Rudy Gobert his flowers, man. The Wolves' defensive rating drops to 97 points per 100 when he's on the court, while rising to 108.6 when he sits. That noted, the Wolves have defenders everywhere you look and they are seriously tied together.

Recent findings suggest that with their four regular starters on the floor (LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, Jonathan Kuminga and Gobert), Minnesota is registering a 92.0 defensive rating with a plus-20.5 net rating. But even when they go smaller and swap in Ayo Dosunmu for Gobert with the other three, the rating stays at 94.2 with a plus-16.2 net.

It has been revealed that no matter the combination, if four of those five guys are on the court, the defense is no worse than 96.0. It's super impressive stuff, and so much for the idea that Ball is a defensive liability. Speaking of Ball ...

The LaMelo effect is being felt in two places: Minnesota, of course, but also Charlotte, where the offense has plummeted from a 123.3 rating with Ball on the court last year to a league-worst 103.1 this season. Being down Kon Knueppel doesn't help, but it's night and day watching this unit try to generate clean looks without Ball's creation and passing.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the Wolves are flying. The defense is carrying the day and we're going to get to some of the guys carrying more impressive statistical weight than Ball, at least relatively, but watch this team play and try to argue his impact isn't all over the floor. He won the game for Minnesota on Tuesday with two defensive plays over the closing seconds.

LaMelo wins the game with back to back defensive plays! Who would have thought? 👀 pic.twitter.com/v9xYpR7eZu.

Of course, his impact is felt most offensively. The pace. Energy. All of Minnesota's shooting percentages go up with Ball on the court, as they did last season in Charlotte, and that's not because of Ball's own shooting. He's only making 41.8% of his own shots, after all. It's his passing, his flow. As fancy as it is, it's fundamental in its contagious, force-multiplying impact.

The bottom line is this: Over his last 53 games between Charlotte and Minnesota, Ball has gone 39-14. That's the pace of a 60-win team. He's an agent of chaos, fine. It can look out of control. He still chucks up the playground shots, often off one foot and from barely inside the boundary. But we all wondered what it would look like when he was playing for a team with real stakes. Is he a winner? Or are his stats empty? Honestly, he's not even that impressive of a stats guy so far. He's just a winner.

The Wolves can deploy uncompromised lineups up and down their roster, meaning they don't have to decide between offense and defense. All their guys do both. They also have multiple offensive weapons even without Edwards, which is why Ball isn't having to carry a bigger scoring burden than he's equipped to handle, at least efficiently.

Recent findings suggest that terrence Shannon Jr. put up 34 off the bench in a win over Portland on Monday. The next night, Dosunmu and McDaniels, who are playing at legit All-Star levels, combined for 52 with nine 3-pointers. Kuminga is giving them 12.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, almost three assists and a steal over 30 minutes per game.

Other than Gobert, Jaylen Clark is really the only truly offensively limited guy, but for the minutes he gets, he is one hell of a defender. You do not want this man guarding you. You do not want anything to do with this team overall.

Recent findings suggest that they came out of the gate looking incredible with Edwards and Ball looking like basketball brothers. It seemed like that was going to die out when Edwards got hurt. It hasn't.

When Edwards gets back, this Timberwolves team has the look of a legitimate contender.

Industry News: Paul George embracing role as second option to Jayson Tatum: 'Not one of those guys that have to have an ego'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The entire basketball world has spent the past five months or so trying to figure out what exactly caused the beef, or, well, lamb chops and gravy, between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.
  • Industry observers note that we know the Celtics tried to trade Brown for Giannis Antetokounmpo.
  • Recent findings suggest that regardless, there are clearly some hard feelings here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The entire basketball world has spent the past five months or so trying to figure out what exactly caused the beef, or, well, lamb chops and gravy, between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. The two coexisted harmoniously as teammates on the Boston Celtics for the better part of a decade. They won a championship together and reached the Eastern Conference Finals five times. That run ended this summer with Boston's stunning decision to swap Brown for Paul George and draft picks, and we've never quite gotten to the bottom of what's happened since.

Industry observers note that we know the Celtics tried to trade Brown for Giannis Antetokounmpo. After moving Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers, Brad Stevens spoke about the team's need to both spread its financial resources and its usage among a wider group of players. Celtics broadcaster Brian Scalabrine claimed that Brown went to the organization with a list of demands that, if not met, would be followed by a trade request. Brown's camp has denied this claim, and Scalabrine himself has walked it back. Marc Spears reported in July that he had heard Brown felt like the Celtics treated Tatum as though he was the organizational favorite.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, there are clearly some hard feelings here. Brown claimed last offseason that the 2025-26 season was his personal favorite as a professional. Tatum missed most of that season, and Brown had his best statistical season. Brown claimed early this season that Tatum has a "hell of a PR team," and then he snubbed him at tip-off before their first game as opponents, a Celtics victory. That game was owned by George, Brown's replacement in Boston.

Industry observers note that so far, the partnership has been harmonious. George is outplaying Brown thus far this season. He's been among the NBA's very best 3-point shooters, has spearheaded a system shift in Boston's defense that has finally allowed the Celtics to generate some turnovers, and he's done so on fewer shot attempts per game (15.7) than Brown has taken in any season since the 2019-20 campaign. Boston's vision for the George fit has proven accurate, and that's been as true in the press as it has been on the court.

Recent findings suggest that george addressed his partnership with Tatum in an interview with The Athletic on Wednesday, and he made it clear that his role is to "help JT," in clear deference to Boston's remaining superstar. "I'm just not one of those guys that have to have an ego," George said. "My ego comes from what I do on the court when the ball gets thrown up and how I impact the game and how I affect the game in all aspects. My ego doesn't have to come from me stroking it or me thinking I'm bigger than someone or better than someone.

Recent findings suggest that "But with that is, I know where I'm at in my career. I'm at the end of my career. Tatum, JT has (many) more years ahead of him, and he's someone that I admired from afar. And to see where he's taken his game, how much better he's gotten and him having all the tools and weapons to be the best player in the league, how can I help that? How can I support that and get him there?".

Recent findings suggest that george and Brown are fundamentally different players. Brown, younger and a better scorer off the dribble, was well-suited to lifting last year's Celtics to a surprising 56-win season despite their shorthanded roster. But George's superior shooting and low-maintenance playing style have suited Tatum perfectly, and the fact that he's at a point in his career in which he's eager to take a backseat to Tatum helps with whatever palace intrigue occurred between Tatum and Brown at the end of their joint run.

It has been revealed that if Brown was indeed frustrated with the idea of playing second fiddle to Tatum, it hasn't shown in Philadelphia. His 76ers are 12-3, he's openly called them Tyrese Maxey's team, and he played a key role in recruiting LeBron James, another ball-dominant star, to join the team in free agency. His usage on this star-studded 76ers roster is at its lowest rate since the 2019-20 season. Clearly, this was not as simple as Brown wanting his own team as so many suggested.

But something created a rift in Boston that led to where we are now, and so far, everyone involved should be happy with how this has played out. The 76ers and Celtics have the two best records in the Eastern Conference. George is playing better in Boston than he ever did in Philadelphia. Tatum is playing better with George than he ever did with Brown. And Brown has become an essential component of a different contender rather than being forced to start from scratch on a bad team as he would have if he'd been traded to the Milwaukee Bucks for Antetokounmpo.

On the court, at least, egos haven't been a problem for anybody, and the deal is working out for everyone.

Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.

England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.

Thomas Tuchel’s side were three goals in front and cruising when Anderson - looking to atone for a sloppy error from Jarrel Quansah - cynically hauled down 19-year-old Yamal as he barrelled down on goal.

Spain were awarded a penalty for the infringement, and Anderson was sent off - much to the Manchester City star’s bemusement.

But Yamal, aggrieved by Anderson’s challenge, made a beeline for the midfielder following the challenge. According to Spanish reports, the attacker mouthed ‘tonto, tonto’ to his rival following his dismissal.

The colloquial term can mean a number of things, varying from idiot, fool or stupid, but in any case is far from a term of affection.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨بطاقة حمراء لإليوت أندرسون ولامين يامال يستفزه🤯🤯#اسبانيا_انجلترا #دوري_الأمم_الأوروبية pic.twitter.com/cOrswp5kCC.

Lamine Yamal was spotted taunting Elliot Anderson after the Manchester City midfielder was sent off for a challenge on the winger.

The moment came in England's historic 3-2 win over the World Champions.

Anderson blanked the 19-year-old while a VAR review confirmed the on-field official’s decision was the right one, eventually trudging off the pitch.

A fired-up Yamal galvanised the reigning world champions as they searched for an unlikely comeback.

Mikel Oyarzabal, the man who scored Spain’s winner against England two years ago in the 2024 Euros final, converted the spot kick before Nico Williams scored Spain’s second after latching on to an excellent Yamal cross.

However, Las Rojas fell short, with Sunday’s defeat their first in an imperious 43-game run.

A jubilant Thomas Tuchel hailed the match as his ‘best performance of my time as manager’.

‘What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,’ Tuchel said after the game. ’Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

‘It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.’.

  • The 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners have acquired third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, the teams declared on Wednesday. The Royals receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller and lefty Jose A. Ferrer in the deal.

Here are the full trade details:.

Garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

The 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

Ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.

Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.

Sources indicate that the Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

Industry observers note that one player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very significant step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, new manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:.

Donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

Industry observers note that the lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

It has been revealed that seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

Before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur showed a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

Recent findings suggest that garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.

Industry observers note that the free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be remarked for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

It has been revealed that evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.

Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:.

Industry observers note that (His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a substantial league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

The Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

Industry observers note that ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

And three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

In a recent development, the Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla called on star forward Jayson Tatum to be "better" after he was called for a controversial technical foul in the closing seconds of Wednesday's 105-101 loss, which effectively sealed the game for the Denver Nuggets.

"We can't put ourselves in that position to even give the refs an opportunity to interpret it a certain type of way," Mazzulla stated after the game. "Gotta be better.".

Recent findings suggest that with 6.4 seconds remaining, Jamal Murray worked off a huge screen from Nikola Jokić, created space with a nasty step-back on Neemias Queta and buried a difficult jumper to give the Nuggets a three-point lead. The Celtics, who had led by as many as 17 late in the first half, still had a chance to tie, however. At least, they did, until Tatum threw the ball toward referee John Goble.

According to recent reports, the baseline official, Eric Dalen, immediately hit Tatum with a technical foul. Murray stepped to the line and made the free throw to put the Nuggets up by four.

It has been revealed that "I told [Dalen], like, I wasn't mad. Wasn't a foul on me; we just called a timeout," Tatum noted. "John Goble called a timeout and pointed at our bench. Thought he was looking this way, but yeah, he called a tech. For me, just find the female ref that was there, or the other ref, and whoever was probably closest, I should have just gave them the ball.".

Jamal Murray hits a clutch jumper to extend the Nuggets the lead to 3, with 6.4 seconds remaining in regulation.The Celtics call a timeout, and Jayson Tatum throws the ball towards the ref John Goble, who wasn't looking, and receives a technical foul, which Murray converts to… pic.twitter.com/PZtzl0zs3D.

Tatum's controversial technical capped a brutal second half for the Celtics and their star.

According to recent reports, after scoring 20 points in the first half to help the Celtics build a 17-point lead, Tatum managed just four points in the second half on 2-of-6 shooting with five turnovers. Notably, he missed mid-range attempts on back-to-back possessions in the final two minutes. The first could have pushed the Celtics' lead back up to three, while the latter would have put them in front.

"The four turnovers I had in the third quarter really put us out of sync," Tatum said. "In those situations, I gotta communicate better, I gotta execute better, I gotta take care of the ball. I think that kinda put us in a hole, and was the turning point for the game.".

This defeat was the first time all season that the Celtics have lost back-to-back games. Now 11-4, the Celtics are 1 ½ games back of the Philadelphia 76ers for the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference. Come April, when seeding battles are heating up, the Celtics may rue this one.

In the second half, as their lead melted away, the Celtics turned the ball over 11 times, were called for 20 fouls (which led to 22 Nuggets free throws) and shot 2 of 19 from 3-point range. Two of the Celtics' four defeats this season have now involved a major blown lead: 22 points against the Detroit Pistons on opening day and 17 points against the Nuggets.

NFL exploring possibility of implementing new travel rules for international games

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that with the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change.
  • In a recent development, the NFL is at the moment exploring a upcoming travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city.
  • According to recent reports, "Presently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that with the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.

In a recent development, the NFL is at the moment exploring a upcoming travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic, NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming.

According to recent reports, "Presently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly mentioned. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at.".

Industry observers note that it's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams. The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture.

Sources indicate that on the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning, leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off.

Recent findings suggest that the Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the proposal backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss.

It has been revealed that if the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday.

According to recent reports, that exact travel strategy was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers, Texans, Colts, and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a newly introduced travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change.

It has been revealed that since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss.

There were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a newly introduced travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route).

Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a newly introduced travel policy is in place for next season.

Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs laying early foundation for one of the best running back careers ever

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery. Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.

Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Latest England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards.

Just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season.

All of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995).

Sources indicate that now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff, a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver (Amon-Ra St. Brown), a Pro Bowl tight end (Sam LaPorta), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle (Penei Sewell), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver (Jameson Williams). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season.

Among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine.

Here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.

Recent findings suggest that week 11 gives Gibbs a chance to deliver an all-time encore performance in a matchup against Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the No. 1 run defense in the NFL (79.2 rushing yards per game allowed) this season. Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vanessa Bryant, the widow of Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant, has denied a report that she is teaming up with two-time Lakers champion Pau Gasol to attempt to purchase the Los Angeles Sparks.
  • In a recent development, "Another rumor out today… I have never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA owner.
  • Sports Business Journal reported on Wednesday that Bryant and Gasol were interested in the Sparks, which were put up for sale in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vanessa Bryant, the widow of Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant, has denied a report that she is teaming up with two-time Lakers champion Pau Gasol to attempt to purchase the Los Angeles Sparks.

In a recent development, "Another rumor out today… I have never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA owner. If that was true I would announce it. I'm just over here undecided on what seasonal coffee flavor I like and over caffeinated," Bryant wrote on Instagram. "I can only speak for myself. I don't know what anyone else does or does not have going on.".

Sports Business Journal reported on Wednesday that Bryant and Gasol were interested in the Sparks, which were put up for sale in October. Owner Mark Walter, who has been shedding assets amid an FBI and SEC investigation into his wealth management firm, is seeking a record-shattering $700 million for the franchise and its yet-unopened practice facility, according to Bloomberg. The current record for a WNBA team sale is $300 million, which Tilman Fertitta paid for the Connecticut Sun before moving the franchise to Houston to revive the Comets.

It has been revealed that notably, Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, who purchased the Lakers from Walter earlier this year, are reportedly uninterested in the Sparks. Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer reportedly considered bidding on the team in 2024, but is presently prohibited for submitting a bid because he is serving a one-year suspension from the NBA over his role in the Aspiration scandal. However, at least one of the groups bidding for the Sparks, a group of investors put together by Swish Partners, would consider moving the team to Ballmer's Intuit Dome.

Gasol already has a financial stake in the WNBA, as he invested in the league's 2022 capital raise. Bryant frequently attends Sparks games and has brought WNBA players in to host clinics at the Mamba & Mambacita Sports Foundation. The late Kobe Bryant was a prominent figure in the women's basketball community, especially coaching his late daughter Gianna's AAU team. Gianna hoped to play for the University of Connecticut and presumably the WNBA afterward before tragically dying in the helicopter accident that killed her father and seven others in 2020.

Sources indicate that several former NBA players own or have owned minority stakes in WNBA teams, including Magic Johnson (Sparks), Dwyane Wade (Chicago Sky), Kyle Lowry (Toronto Tempo) and Grant Hill and Chris Webber (the upcoming Detroit expansion team set to begin play in 2029). However, no former NBA player holds the governorship of a WNBA team. Gasol could change that. If we expand to immediate family, Bryant could become the first spouse of a former NBA player to hold a controlling interest in a WNBA team, though at this stage, the exact structure of a possible Bryant-Gasol bid and the other investors who could be involved are not clear.

I don't know whether the Carolina Hurricanes have an ample supply of ibuprofen or Pedialyte, but there has been no Stanley Cup hangover in Raleigh. In fact, the reigning champions look even better than they did at this time last year.

The Hurricanes own the NHL's best record at 16-3-2, and they're outpacing last year's performance, even when you factor in two extra regular season games. Carolina played an 84-game pace of 115 points last season. The team is tracking for 136 points in 2026-27.

It's not just that the Canes are winning. It's how they're winning. Carolina is bludgeoning its opponents to the tune of a plus-40 goal differential, which leads the league. The next closest team is the Edmonton Oilers at plus-30.

In a recent development, if you're looking for an area in which the Canes don't excel, good luck. They rank second in goals scored (87), first in goals allowed (47), eighth in power play (25.4%) and fifth in penalty kill (85.9%). Under the hood, Carolina is far and away the best team in five-on-five expected goals share at 62.0%.

Concerns about goaltending have been quelled by Pyotr Kochetkov, who's saved 7.64 goals above average while posting a .920 save percentage. Up front, Carolina's scoring depth is unmatched, and the defensive corps is nearly impenetrable.

As the Hurricanes tighten their grip on the No. 1 spot, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

#73461. Industry News: Ranking the NBA's most hopeless teams: Which franchise is in the bleakest situation? And who can't fix it?

Industry News: Ranking the NBA's most hopeless teams: Which franchise is in the bleakest situation? And who can't fix it?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2141 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Milwaukee Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo as an opponent for the first time on Wednesday, and it didn't go well.
  • Recent findings suggest that the question here is how bleak.
  • Sources indicate that to be clear here, we are operating in terms of championship equity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Milwaukee Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo as an opponent for the first time on Wednesday, and it didn't go well. Though the final score showed only a seven-point margin, the Miami Heat led by 26 after three quarters and were never in much danger. The defeat dropped the Bucks to 1-14 on the season. The greatest player in their franchise's history now wears another jersey, and they're at the beginning of what figures to be a very long rebuild. Things are bleak.

Recent findings suggest that the question here is how bleak. Milwaukee knew it would spend this season in the cellar. It probably expects to live there for a few years. But how far away from winning seriously are the Bucks really? Are they further from genuine contention than any other team in the NBA? Who, right now, has the bleakest long-term outlook?

Sources indicate that to be clear here, we are operating in terms of championship equity. We don't care if you have a chance to be a plucky .500 team. No, the barometer we're using here is how likely each team is to reach a conference finals in the next five seasons. We're accounting not only for players on the existing roster, but long-term financial flexibility, available draft assets and the competence of the front office helming these organizations. With all of that in mind, let's rank the NBA's most hopeless long-term outlooks.

The broad sentiment following their punishment for circumventing the salary cap with Kawhi Leonard was that the Clippers faced the bleakest future in the entire NBA. That's probably overstating things slightly.

Remember, we're talking about a Los Angeles team here. Someone, inevitably, is going to want to play for them. All it takes is one player bucking the league-wide trend against superstar free agency and they're back in business. They have an owner who will spare no expense in pursuit of wins, and there's a 26-year-old All-Star in Darius Garland already on the roster. Couple that with the hope generated by No. 5 overall pick Keaton Wagler, and while the path here is extremely narrow, it exists. If the Brooklyn Nets could build a contender without draft picks in the late 2010s, it's theoretically possible for the Clippers to do the same.

It has been revealed that of course, the Nets weren't subject to that league-wide pivot away from free agency. They didn't have to trade picks to get Kevin Durant or Kyrie Irving in the door. It's much, much harder nowadays to import talent like that without sacrificing picks that the Clippers frankly don't have. The five first-round picks they were docked in the Leonard investigation left them fully Stepien-locked: while they will have (not especially valuable) first-round picks in odd-numbered years moving forward, they can't trade any of them yet.

Industry observers note that there's also the reputational hit the Clippers just took. Will players interested in winning want to risk their careers on a team that cheated? Can the Clippers even appeal to such players given their asset deficit? These are going to be real hurdles. Their path to the conference finals might rely on a star who's not especially competitive. After all, anyone serious about winning could find a team closer to doing so.

In a recent development, they're a blank slate with one very promising prospect. Darius Acuff is putting up star box-score numbers in his rookie season. That's by no means a guarantee of future stardom, of course. He's as inefficient as you'd expect a rookie to be on this volume. He's taking more shots per game than Jalen Brunson, Tyrese Maxey or Dwyane Wade ever did over a full season. But Acuff has a path to becoming one of the NBA's best offensive point guards. These aren't totally empty calories.

Industry observers note that there's nothing else here. No other notable prospects aside from a handful of likely long-term bench youngsters (Dylan Cardwell, Maxime Raynaud, Emanuel Sharp). Sacramento mostly controls its own picks (aside from the 2031 swap it inexplicably gave San Antonio in the DeMar DeRozan sign-and-trade), but that means less than it used to in the lottery reform era. Its books slowly clean up in the offseasons to come, with Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter expiring after this season and Domantas Sabonis and Malik Monk joining them in the summer of 2028, but Sacramento's forays into cap space have typically been unsuccessful. This isn't exactly a desirable destination. That's what happens when you miss the playoffs 19 times in 20 years.

That's what separates Sacramento from fellow "one possible star, otherwise blank slate" candidates like the Chicago Bulls. With the hire of Bryson Graham to run basketball operations, the Bulls at least appear to be trending towards becoming a normal organization. Normalcy has eternally eluded Sacramento. The burden of proof is on the Kings. When you've been a mess for 20 years, it's on you to prove that you've cleaned up your act. We'll trust the Kings when they've earned it and not a second sooner.

For now, they can at least start by actually keeping their success stories in the building. They've kept only one first-round pick this decade through the end of his rookie contract: Keegan Murray, who is now pretty substantially overpaid. Meanwhile, Tyrese Haliburton has blossomed into a superstar in Indiana, while their entire 2021 draft class (Davion Mitchell and Neemias Queta) now starts for Eastern Conference championship hopefuls. They had the unanimous Coach of the Year and the Executive of the Year and fired both within two years. The Kings can't help themselves.

There's far more talent in the cupboard here than in Sacramento, but the same organizational concerns apply. The Joe Dumars regime makes mistakes -- the two-year minimum for DeAndre Jordan, not waiting until after the 2025 Finals to trade Indiana its 2026 pick back, everything Shamit Dua has reported about the infamous Derik Queen trade -- that typical teams would never dream of.

According to recent reports, there is not a discernible plan here besides, seemingly, "acquire players who can put the ball through the hoop." There are a lot of decent individual creators on this roster. None of them synergize well because so few of them can consistently make 3s and all of them are on-ball players with stylistic clashes. The Pelicans have seemingly made the determination, for instance, that Queen cannot play significant minutes alongside Zion Williamson. That's a reasonable choice... but then why is Williamson still on the team? Or, if the Pelicans view him as a fixture, why make such a risky trade for Queen in the first place?

The trickle-down effect of putting all of these dribblers on the same team is that none of them seem happy to be on it. Dejounte Murray asked for a trade. Jordan Poole is making googly eyes at the Warriors. Trey Murphy has reportedly signaled a desire to move. What is the blueprint here? What kind of team are the Pelicans trying to build? What do they view as their path to genuine winning?

That's what distinguishes Newly introduced Orleans from Sacramento. If the Kings get a few more high draft picks and use them on players that complement Acuff, I'd see the vision. It would require Acuff becoming an All-NBA scorer and those picks hitting, but I see the sort of teams they could build, even if they're unlikely to actually do so. I have no earthly idea what the Pelicans would do with a few high picks because talent is not at the moment the problem. It's how they're using and nurturing it. It's just hard to envision a team with so little understanding of how to balance skill sets and bring out the best in their players making a serious playoff push. Something significant in the organization would have to change.

In a recent development, they're the best team on this list in the present, and they've clawed their way back to .500 after a miserable start that included leaks about the team's lack of a point guard. Again, we're dealing in upside here. That's what the Suns lack.

Industry observers note that they control none of their own first-round picks in the seven-year tradable window except for their 2032 selection... which is frozen because they spent the 2024-25 season above the second apron. Even if they had picks, the Suns under Matt Ishbia have never displayed any discipline in using them. Ishbia traded nearly a full draft for Kevin Durant mere days after acquiring the team, spent an unprotected 2031 pick on three far lesser choices that amounted to Mark Williams and a Jusuf Nurkić cap dump, and then spent their 2033 pick as soon as they could access it to get Miles Bridges, whom they've been meaningfully better without thus far this season.

According to recent reports, the most talented players here are all right around their physical peaks. Devin Booker is 30. Dillon Brooks turns 31 this season, and Bridges turns 29. They're going to get worse, not better, and without draft picks, their means of replacing them are minimal. Even the diamonds they've dug out of the rough are on the older side. Collin Gillespie is 27. Jordan Goodwin is 28. The truly young players, like Khaman Maluach and Rasheer Fleming, have thus far underwhelmed. The younger, star-level talent here is Jalen Green, who plays Booker's position and has been a disaster on both ends this season. Why exactly is he still starting over Gillespie? Are the Suns just trying to salvage his trade value?

Teams like the Clippers, Kings and Pelicans are at least young enough and financially flexible enough to grow. The Suns, at least from an asset and financial standpoint, are essentially all-in on a Play-In-caliber roster. That Play-In-caliber roster is going to get worse as it gets older and more expensive and, without access to top talent in the draft, replenishing it is going to be borderline impossible.

Sources indicate that the Bucks cherry-pick traits from all of our other selections. The Clippers circumvented the cap; the Bucks are getting investigated for doing so with Gary Trent Jr. The Pelicans have a roster full of overlapping skill sets; the Bucks have a million shooting guards, which made the decision to re-sign Trent for $64 million all the stranger. The Suns don't control any of their own picks and the Bucks won't until 2031 at the earliest. The Kings have the NBA's least-successful owner in Vivek Ranadivé, while the Bucks may have the NFL's in Jimmy Haslam, though he technically won't become governor until 2028 due to Milwaukee's bizarre ownership structure (another point against them, as successful teams tend to have stable leadership rather than rotating five-year terms).

Who is going to be the best player on the team in five years? Brayden Burries is the best long-term prospect, but he profiles as more of a high-end role player. Tyler Herro was an All-Star in the sense that Norman Powell and D'Angelo Russell were All-Stars: they put up major numbers in a weak Eastern Conference. Kel'El Ware was the lottery ticket from the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade and he's been so bad that he's somehow playing less than he did on a Heat team that was trying to win. Without access to their own picks or a market that tends to draw free agents, they're basically hoping someone internal (Nate Ament? Ryan Rollins?) breaks out or that they hit on a pick far later than you should rely on.

According to recent reports, you could argue that just by virtue of being in the Eastern Conference, the Bucks have a cleaner path to the final four than those West teams do because they don't have to worry about Victor Wembanyama or the specter of healthier versions of the Oklahoma City Thunder down the line. That's fair, but as we've seen this year, injuries loom over every season. You know what else the West has aside from those two juggernauts? The four other teams on this list. The Bucks, by a wide margin, are the most hopeless team in their own conference. They're starting from the absolute bottom.

This was potentially avoidable. Had they acted sooner and traded Antetokounmpo in 2025 when the whole world knew a deal was eventually coming, they could have secured a stronger return and set themselves up for a quicker turnaround. Alas, the Bucks chose to waive-and-stretch Damian Lillard, locking them into $22.5 million in dead money through the end of the decade so they could sign Myles Turner to a contract that is increasingly looking like $28 million or so per year in... close to dead money. Milwaukee got its championship in 2021, but at this rate, it's going to be a while before it sniffs another one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Star Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered one of the most unfortunate injuries of the NFL season when he tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of Fresh England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye early in the Lions' win over the Pats in Munich, Germany.
  • According to recent reports, hutchinson brought Maye to the ground and then jumped into the air in celebration.
  • Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room.(📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered one of the most unfortunate injuries of the NFL season when he tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of Fresh England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye early in the Lions' win over the Pats in Munich, Germany.

According to recent reports, hutchinson brought Maye to the ground and then jumped into the air in celebration. He tore his knee when he landed.

Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room.(📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF.

In a recent development, hutchinson is out for the remainder of the season, dealing a significant blow to the Lions' hopes of making a run through the playoffs. On Thursday, Hutchinson released a statement about the injury, his recovery and his future celebration plans via his Instagram account.

In a recent development, "I honestly can't believe it. I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me," Hutchinson wrote. "But even something like this won't hold me back.".

In the wake of the injury, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo remarked that he's retiring his backflip celebration because of what happened to Hutchinson. And now, Hutchinson himself says he won't be jumping in the air in celebration anymore, either.

Sources indicate that "Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger," Hutchinson stated. "2. That's the last time I go airborne 😁👍".

Hutchinson getting injured while celebrating his sack meant that he joined a sneakily extensive list of players suffering unusually-timed injuries, such as Lamarr Houston, Stephen Tulloch and Bill Gramatica, each of whom also tore their ACL while celebrating a play.

Hutchinson's injury probably won't stop everyone in the league from celebrating in the air, but if it inspires even a few more players to stop going airborne, that'll probably be for the best.

For what it's worth, Lions coach Dan Campbell remarked that even in the wake of Hutchinson being lost for the season, he won't tell his players to stop celebrating on the field.

According to recent reports, "I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore,'" Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket.

Campbell also recalled a story from his own playing days while again stating that he won't tell players to stop celebrating their on-field accomplishments.

"No, I don't believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself," Campbell remarked. "We're not talking to 8-year-olds here. And I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play, and I freaking pumped my arm up and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm.

"This game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not.".

Industry observers note that campbell is a firm believer in building the personality of your team. It's clear that he doesn't want to change his team's personality — which has been built in his own image over the years — even in the wake of a devastating injury.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The hot stove is starting to heat up.
  • We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up.
  • The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team declared on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the vital offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team declared on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

Fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a big dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

The Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

According to recent reports, skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are mentioned to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

Star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

According to recent reports, seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

It has been revealed that on Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

Sources indicate that after signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow mentioned it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

Breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster challenges remaining this offseason.

Sources indicate that free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

Although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

Sources indicate that the Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

Still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

Sources indicate that veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

It has been revealed that pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.

The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a newly introduced low point.

Sources indicate that the Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures. While Chicago's biggest issue has come on the defensive end this season, the Bulls haven't exactly been lighting opponents up offensively, sitting 23rd in the league in offensive rating.

The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.

Sources indicate that "I've been in the league for 13 years... that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of."Julius Randle didn't hold back after the Nets’ 30-point loss to Bulls. 😳 pic.twitter.com/s3YQ8TxP35.

In a recent development, "The main struggle? I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle noted after the game. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes -- it's just a bad night -- but it's how we did it. That just, it wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We gotta find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just is unacceptable.".

Considering Randle has been on his fair share of bad basketball teams over his career in Los Angeles, Latest Orleans and New York, that's saying something.

There are five teams that have separated themselves from the pack at the bottom of the NBA in terms of defense and the Nets are one of them with a 119.0 defensive rating (26th in the league). No one expected much of Brooklyn on that end of the floor with the roster they've assembled, but it's one thing to have lesser talent on the defensive end; it's another to combine that with a general lack of effort.

This early in the season, the latter is a much larger concern and the Nets have now given up at least 124 points in five of their last six games. If they were able to shrug off some of those lopsided losses to quality teams as life in the NBA, Wednesday was proof that their problems extend far beyond just some schedule losses.

According to recent reports, giving up 137 to a Bulls team that's been similarly bad this year is, in Randle's words, unacceptable. The concern is that no one in Brooklyn, including Randle, seems quite sure what the exact problem is or how to fix it.

#73455. Latest Update: In Kansas City, Kenneth Walker III and the run game makes the Chiefs contenders again

Latest Update: In Kansas City, Kenneth Walker III and the run game makes the Chiefs contenders again

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that over the last two years, the Kansas City Chiefs had a significant problem: they could not create massive plays.
  • It has been revealed that the Chiefs were once arguably the most explosive offense in the NFL.
  • Over the years, defenses started playing the Chiefs much differently in the latter part of the Tyreek Hill era, especially after Hill left the team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that over the last two years, the Kansas City Chiefs had a significant problem: they could not create massive plays. In 2024 and 2025, Kansas City generated a gain of 20-plus yards on just 4.8% of its offensive plays, according to Tru Media, a rate that ranked tied for 29th in the NFL.

It has been revealed that the Chiefs were once arguably the most explosive offense in the NFL. Between 2018 (Patrick Mahomes' first full season as the starter) and 2023, the Chiefs created an explosive play on 7.2% of their offensive plays, second-place and just 0.1% behind the league-leading San Francisco 49ers.

Over the years, defenses started playing the Chiefs much differently in the latter part of the Tyreek Hill era, especially after Hill left the team. They prioritized shutting down explosive passing plays with two-high coverages and daring the Chiefs to march the ball downfield with short passes and runs. And for the most part, the Chiefs were able to do just that.

Kansas City ranked second in the NFL in success rate (50.5%) between 2021 (Hill's final season with the Chiefs) and 2023, according to TruMedia, checking in first in passing success rate despite a lower explosive-play rate and a respectable 13th in rushing success rate. In 2024 and 2025, the Chiefs' success rate dropped to 48.5%, and they dropped to 12th in passing success rate and 14th in rushing success rate. Their inability to create explosive plays on the ground or through the air limited their ability to generate positive gains on shorter plays.

In a recent development, defenses were particularly unthreatened by Kansas City's ability to run the ball. With a post-injury Isaiah Pacheco and an aging Kareem Hunt in the backfield, the Chiefs simply could not create big plays on the ground, and defenses didn't much care if they wanted to plod along at around three-and-a-half yards per carry. They were, in fact, quite happy to let the Chiefs burn plays on those piddling gains, setting up Patrick Mahomes and the passing game in disadvantageous down-and-distance situations.

According to recent reports, faced with this problem, the Chiefs finally made a significant investment in their running back room, targeting one of the NFL's most explosive backs by signing Kenneth Walker III to a three-year, $43.05 million contract in free agency. Between 2022 and 2025, Walker ranked seventh in the NFL in explosive run rate among the 34 running backs with at least 500 carries, according to TruMedia — and he was 0.3% away from third place on that list.

In a recent development, the investment has paid off beyond the Chiefs' wildest dreams. The Chiefs have soared from dead last in the NFL in explosive run rate in 2024 and 2025 to third in 2026. Between Walker and backup Emmett Johnson, the Chiefs already have more explosive runs by running backs this season than they did in the last two years combined, according to Tru Media. Kansas City has done all that without sacrificing down-to-down efficiency, which was at least a minor concern with Walker.

The Chiefs' rate of negative-yard runs has barely moved this year, while their rates of five-plus-yard runs and explosive runs have, well, exploded. As a result, their yards-per-carry average has jumped from 31st in the league to first, and their EPA per-play average on rushing attempts has jumped from 14th in the league to first.

And it really is largely due to the running backs. The offensive line is creating a bit more yardage before contact, according to TruMedia, but the differential pales in comparison to the difference in yards after contact, and especially in avoided tackle rate.

Walker, in particular, is seemingly able to generate explosive runs out of thin air. He can do it by getting skinny in the hole and then bursting through for a significant gain. He's not necessarily known for this, but it reveals up all over his tape.

Sources indicate that he can do it by pressing the hole and then, when he sees nothing available in the designed gap, bouncing it to the outside and beating oncoming defenders—whether they be linebackers or defensive backs—to the corner and scooting right past them to the end zone. How many times have we seen him do something like this this year?

It has been revealed that both he and Johnson can spot the cutback lanes when the front side gets clogged up. They have the vision, and especially the quickness, to make a hard stop and cut, or jump from one hole to the next and beat defenders to the spot. We've seen this repeatedly throughout the season.

Johnson is also just extremely slippery. You can't get him down with the first tackler. He just shakes the guy in front of him, whether with a juke, a cut, a shrug-off, or something else. And then he makes the second and third guy work to bring him down to the ground as well.

Industry observers note that and of course, Walker can put all of those things together on one run. He'll bounce it to the outside, shake off a tackler, cut back, break another tackle, and then keep gaining yards. Some of the moves he strings together are almost comical.

These two backs creating yardage on their own have been a massive boon to Kansas City's offense. The Chiefs were 11th in EPA per play across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and they're fifth so far this year. They're fifth in success rate and first in yards per play, as well.

Sources indicate that and that's all true despite the fact that they have been without their starting left tackle all season, have benched one of their guards for disciplinary reasons in two different games, and failed to add any talent to the pass-catching corps until they traded for Josh Downs last week. It's been almost entirely about the run game, and specifically about the guys running the ball.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday confirmed they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the Fresh York Post.

In a recent development, skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

Gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

In a recent development, CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

Industry observers note that gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, significant movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

Sources indicate that gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.
